messages:
maria: Heads-up — reproducible perf regression in paged-attn after switching the kernel selector default to `flash-v3` for long sequences (>2048). Quick numbers: flash-v2 = 124 ms, flash-v3 = 152 ms on A100 bf16 batch=8. Repro steps below.

sam: Can you paste the profile/flamegraph? Is it kv pager thrashing or kernel-launch overhead?

maria: Paste of perf-summary + notes:```
perf: cycles: 1.2e9
CPU: user 12s, sys 4s
GPU memcpy async wait: 28ms spike
kv_page_faults: 134 -> spike correlated with requests
TLB_L2_misses: +37%
Kernel launches per request: flash-v2=18, flash-v3=32
```
Observations: more small kernel launches with flash-v3 and higher async copy stalls. Also block-table walk latency increased. Hypothesis: flash-v3 fused path has finer-grained kernels which interact badly with our page prefetch/kv pager heuristics.

oliver: That matches something I saw: flash-v3 changed the microbatching boundary so per-token microkernels are more frequent. Could be tripping our batching hysteresis and causing the pager to delay prefetch until too late.

dave: Can we try overriding `kernel_route` to force flash-v2 and re-run the same trace to confirm?

maria: Did that earlier this morning — with `kernel_route=force:flash-v2` same binary/config: 126 ms and pager backlog dropped significantly. Logs show the KV cache warms roughly 3x faster on v2. When flash-v3 is used, the cold-miss ramp lasts longer (more async transfers queued).

raj: Two angles: allocation pattern and IO. flash-v3 seems to allocate more transient pinned buffers leading to slab fragmentation in our GPU-side allocator. Could be a wear-leveling effect in the slab arena that increases page faults. Recommend trying hybrid allocator and enabling prefault condensation.

maria: Did a quick fused-attn microbench to isolate kernel behavior (seq=4096, heads=32): flash-v2 stable, flash-v3 shows 18% tail increase when `kv_page_faults` > 1/s. Repro command I used:```bash
./bench_paged_attn --seq 4096 --batch 8 --kernel flash-v3 --kv-pages 512 --alloc-policy hybrid
```

bench-bot: CI run 3845009999-PR-8212: microbench passed, but long-seq e2e smoke flaky :eyes:. Full logs: https://ci.redwood.example/builds/3845009999

sam: Proposed action items:
1) Add a telemetry counter for kernel-launch count per request (to see correlation with pager stalls).
2) Implement a quick prefetch heuristic: trigger KV prefetch when the batcher sees > X inflight tokens or when expected kernel-launchs > Y in the next 50ms.
3) Test hybrid allocator with wear-leveling toggled and measure slab fragmentation / page fault rates.
I'll pick up items 1+2. @oliver can you take 3?

oliver: On it — I'll flip the wear-leveling flag and run a 12-hour overnight smoke across seq 2048-8192. I'll collect slab histograms and TLB metrics.

maria: Saving traces + heap snapshots to /tmp/paged-traces/3845009999.tar.gz (contains perf, nvprof, slab histogram). If anyone can eyeball slab fragmentation numbers or spot allocator hot paths, ping me.

dave: Also, let's add an experiment to the kernel selector: prefer kernels with lower kernel-launch count if pager is active (cheap heuristic) — might be a temporary mitigation.

raj: Good call. If flash-v3 brings performance benefits normally, we want a dynamic fallback to flash-v2 only when pager/backpressure signals are present.

maria: Thanks team. I'll attach a minimal repro script and the perf artifacts to the PR. Please comment on PR-8212 if you run the overnight job. :thumbsup:
